subject: Nanotechnology
title: Focused Ion Beam Milling
description: A short lesson to help you apply Focused Ion Beam Milling.

hook.text: A focused ion beam is a nanoscale scalpel — it carves material away atom by atom where you aim it.

buildup.text: Gallium ions are accelerated and focused to a spot a few nanometers wide, sputtering surface atoms away.

discovery.text: FIB can cut cross-sections through finished chips — revealing hidden layers for failure analysis.

twist.text: Gallium atoms implant into the sample and damage it — the surgery leaves scars that must be accounted for.

climax.text: FIB is essential for debugging prototype chips — engineers slice and image without destroying the whole wafer.

punchline.text: An ion scalpel lets engineers perform surgery on chips.

quiz.question: What is a common use of focused ion beam milling?
options: Cross-sectioning finished chips for failure analysis
